Reykin stood in the marshal yard, of the Thorac trading compound. The old Hag stood at his side, hobbled over, his rheumy old eyes still seeing everything. The walled compound was made up of twenty warehouses, three towers, a kitchen and six dormitories. It was home to over six thousand Thorac. The compound sat between the Great Roost, and the Southern Forest. It was a marshal yard, and home, for thousands of Thorac, who joined the Hag. Reykin was a Caravaneer. Head trader for ten wagons, a position held, only by those twenty five years, or older.

The Hag had called all the trade caravans together, and all of them had returned to the compound. A great tent city, of laagered caravans, surrounded the compound. So many Thorac in one place, it was said that together, the caravans held all the goods in Gaea. One of everything at least, but Reykin knew this to be untrue. The Hag had held a meeting, with all the Caravaneers, and had appointed Reykin and nine others as scribes. Each was to be charged with a column of caravans. One thousand caravans to a column.

So Reykin had stood with the Hag, and nine other scribes, as column after column of Thorac caravans had entered the yard. The sun had risen, and climbed high into the sky, and begun to wane, and still the wagons came. Warehouse after warehouse was emptied, wagon after wagon was filled. The sun ran out, before the wagons ran out. So they had slept, and begun once more, with the rising sun. Wheel after wheel had scarred the yard, and still the wagons came. Ten days they loaded the wagons, ten days the warehouses gave up there treasure, ten days Reykin stood. On the eleventh day, the Thorac rested. On the twelfth day, a young girl stood with them. A strange and beautiful creature, with a smile upon her lips.

The Thorac were well dressed, in heavy furs and boots, with thick cloaks, they sweated in the sun. Mile upon mile of wagons, all lined up. In the middle of the yard, stood the strange girl, and a dark circle. The hag began to lead, and the Thorac followed, through the dark vortex they went. Reykin followed, a step behind the Hag, one moment the sun beat down upon him, the next. Well the next almost made him go crazy. Reykin stumbled, a world of whiteness assaulted his senses. Freezing cold, biting hard. The Hag grabbed hold of Reykin, and helped him up, 'welcome to our new outpost son', said the old Hag.
